original_card.question: Can one misleading historical-current claim or missing research cross-reference be corrected?
methods: Trace one confusing path from onboarding to its authoritative source.
Index one tightly related family of obstructions with explicit excluded and open hypotheses.
original_card.acceptance_gate: Produce evidence-backed navigation, preserve historical records and avoid a duplicate global survey.

first_step.inspect: Follow one link from the selected record to its review and compare a potentially stale historical claim.
first_step.scope: Positive control / source-bound orientation only; this is not a new construction or full cold replay.

original_card.first_experiment: Repair one confusing path or produce a scoped map of one related obstruction family.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Clear navigation lowers entry cost for central research; a global survey without a concrete fix is not required.
allowed_variations: One historical-current ambiguity or one bounded family index.
scope_change_triggers: Rewriting frozen scientific packages just to change their historical wording.

actual_scope: One bounded family index: lower bounds on the number of paid calls s that a unit for W complex arrays needs at small block sizes m, each in a stated game, and the smallest shapes (W in s) they leave open. In the engine game of my Lean engine (calls C_v, shifts, invertible XOR-linear address maps, phases i^(z.x+c), rational mixing with scratch; correct at every digit width): block 2 needs 2W and block 3 needs 14W/5 (proved in Lean), block 4 needs 41W/13 (checked by computer), blocks from 4 on need 2.9447 per array (argued by hand). Also: block 3 without phase letters needs 3W for every address group; one array needs m calls and two or more need max(W + m, 2W) in every game with bounded free steps (argued by hand). The README answers two questions in David Harvey's note on the proposed o(n log n) algorithm (one array; 4 arrays at block 3 need 12 calls). The registered check re-derives the certificate numbers, the Lean certificate data and every figure in the tables from package data.
scope_change_reason: The card's method 'Index one tightly related family of obstructions with explicit excluded and open hypotheses' fits, but this package also adds bounds that are not on main (14W/5 at m = 3 in the engine game, 41W/13 at m = 4, the bound from m = 4 on, the no-phase m = 3 bound, W + m and 2W in games with bounded free steps), so it is more than navigation. Each is stated with its game and status, and the predecessors (#288, #2108, the bit-side small-register packages) are credited and quoted rather than rewritten.
bottleneck_link: A single small complex unit with s < Wm would give a large complex-side saving (ln(mW/s)/ln m, for example 6.28e-2 for 5 in 14 at m = 3). The bounds say where such a unit cannot exist and list the smallest shapes where it still could, so that searches start there; none of them changes κ.
stop_rule: Post results already public in my repository with a status no stronger than there, plus the short answers to David Harvey's note in README section 7 (each labelled argued by hand, or checked by verify.py); every figure re-derived by verify.py; every control rejected; Lean statements quoted verbatim from the files; no new search, Lean build or reviewer round for this package.
evidence: verify.py --part main (standard library, about 2 s): sha256 of every data file; block 2: caps <= 4 by exact Z[i] vectors in all 3 directions and attained, demand >= 8; block 3: caps <= 80 by 200 exact vectors in all 7 directions and attained (rank mod p), demand >= 224 by a certified 224 x 224 minor and by the rank of the whole 280 x 280 block, two calls in a row <= 144 by 136 exact vectors, the character block M_0 of rank >= 28 in two formats by two routines; the eight 28 x 28 blocks of the Lean data file Dem3Data.lean times the formula matrix equal the identity mod 65537 (the check Lean's kernel ran); the face certificate of the no-phase bound (cap 8 in 7 directions, demand 24 in all 28 bases, exact over Q(i)); the block-4 arithmetic 27,456 / 86,592 / 41/13 and the format of the 5,412 x 5,412 certificate; the inputs of section 7: two and three moves in independent directions raise the block-4 hook by at least 48,576 and 68,320 (the hook split over the untouched address bits into ranks of at most 280 x 280 mod p; the same split gives the cap 27,456 and block 3's 80 and 144), the exact block-5 and block-6 bounds 834241/278850 and 1188222/399685 from that profile, and the format of the two minor certificates for 48,576 and 68,320 (their determinants on all 16 characters are author evidence); the width-1 zero-call program for C^(x)3 and its failure at width 2; every saving and exclusion in README sections 1 and 6. verify.py --part controls: 20 corrupted certificates and false claims, each rejected. Outside this repository: the Lean proofs (block2_bound, block3_bound, dem3, hook_kept, hook_cap, engine_lower_bound; three standard axioms; a negative control rejected) the hour-long C check of the block-4 determinant (author-evidence/check_m0.c), and the 42-minute C check of the two minor certificates for 48,576 and 68,320 on all 16 characters (author-evidence/check_mj.c, outputs out_check_m4_g2.txt and out_check_m4_g3.txt).
author: Jacob Sussman
ai_assistance: Substantial AI assistance: the programs, checks, proofs, Lean files and texts were written by AI agents (Anthropic Claude) under my direction. The Lean proofs are checked by Lean's kernel; the other proofs were checked only by AI reviewers, as each status says. No independent human review of this package is claimed.

open_questions.question: Is there a 5 in 14 at block 3 in the engine game (saving 6.28e-2)? It sits exactly on the hook bound (14 x 80 = 5 x 224).
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the only block-3 shape with five arrays that the bound proved in Lean leaves open, and the largest block-3 saving still possible.
open_questions.first_step: Decide one sector of the S8 sub-game of my repository's idea-rounds section exactly, one representative per symmetry orbit, judging each candidate by its per-array end condition at width 6 rather than by the cheap tests.

open_questions.question: Is there a 2 in 7 at block 4 (saving 9.63e-2)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: It is the smallest open shape at any block; with private ends the best certificate known leaves room of only 640 out of 137,280.
open_questions.first_step: An exact search confined to address maps in the middle of the program and phase letters between calls (with letters only at the ends, and no mixing between the end letters, it is excluded); in parallel, the finite-group form of the best-bound relaxation at block 3, then at block 4, looking for a certificate above 3.5 calls per array.

open_questions.question: In games whose free steps may mix neighbouring digit columns, is there a 2 in 5 or a 3 in 6 at block 3 (exactly on max(W + 3, 2W))?
open_questions.why_it_matters: There the best bound is only max(W + m, 2W), so a saving up to 3.69e-1 is not excluded.
open_questions.first_step: Finish the third-layer case split of the W + m argument for W = 2, s = m + 2, which would close 2 in 5 there and 2 in 7 at block 5.

open_questions.question: Does 14W/5 hold in #288's full register model, settling its open m = 3 cases (W = 2, s = 5 with two or more inserted free elements; W = 3, s = 8)?
open_questions.why_it_matters: #288 and #2108 left these open; they are excluded in the engine game, but I have not checked that #288's model sits inside it.
open_questions.first_step: List the free elements #288's full register model allows and check that each keeps the block-3 hook; every map that sends one address to one address and acts the same on every column does.

open_questions.question: Can the Lean statements be extended to complex mixing, the widened game and block 4?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Complex mixing and Harvey's B-calls are argued by hand from the Lean proof; 41W/13 rests on a computer-checked certificate.
open_questions.first_step: Change the mixing letter's matrix from rational to complex (one proof step uses it). For 41W/13, split the 16 character blocks further by the bit-swap group and time Lean's kernel on one block before committing.
open_questions.blocked_by: A Lean build of the block-3 files needs about 10 GB of memory.

open_questions.question: At blocks 5 and 6: is there a 2 in 7 (block 5), a 2 in 8 (block 6), or a 3 in 9 at either block?
open_questions.why_it_matters: These would save 2.22e-1 to 3.87e-1; 3 in 9 is not excluded by any bound I know.
open_questions.first_step: Write the third-layer argument for '2 in m + 2 is impossible' in the two small games where the top two levels alone admit a 2 in 5; for 3 in 9, look for a certificate above 3 calls per array at block 5, starting with the best-bound relaxation restricted to frames within distance 2 of the start and of the target.
